decision.summary: 14 of 15 findings are evidence-backed; 1 were insufficient and recorded for follow-up.

findings.statement: NVIDIA's data‑center portfolio comprises accelerated compute, systems, networking, and software.
The public NVIDIA data‑center product catalog is available at https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/products/.
NVIDIA's AI software ecosystem includes CUDA and AI software libraries, runtimes, and developer tools.
United States and Europe are listed as current markets for NVIDIA's data‑center offerings.

Broadcom’s VMware software is sold under a per‑core subscription model. The VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) tier is listed at $200–$400 per core per year, while the VMware Virtual Fabric (VVF) tier is listed at $100–$200 per core per year. A median enterprise contract value is reported as $27,598 per year.

findings.statement: Intel Corp: The Intel Gaudi 3 AI accelerator is scheduled to be available to OEMs—including Dell Technologies, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Lenovo and Supermicro—in the second quarter of 2024.
AMD surpassed Intel in data center processor revenue in Q3 2024, indicating a recent shift in market share between the two rivals in the AI/compute segment.
North America, driven by the United States, leads the global data center chip market, reflecting strong demand and momentum for AI accelerators in the US.
EU regulatory frameworks such as the AI Act, GDPR, DSA, and DMA are cited as perceived barriers that could deter investment in AI accelerator technologies in Europe.

The European Commission’s EuroStack initiative seeks to develop a sovereign tech infrastructure—including semiconductors and computing—to strengthen local capacity for AI accelerators and reduce reliance on foreign cloud providers.
A proposed European sovereign tech fund with an initial €10 billion investment aims to boost digital sovereignty, which could fund the adoption and development of AI accelerator hardware in Europe.
AI developers note that NVIDIA H100 rental costs roughly $1.40 per hour, with longer‑term deals exceeding $2.40 per hour, indicating price sensitivity.
Chip shortages keep NVIDIA H100 prices high, leading AI labs to continue purchasing proven hardware despite limited supply.
The NVIDIA H100 GPU’s 700 W power consumption is highlighted as a concern compared with low‑power alternatives.
Developers share detailed NVIDIA H100 architecture specifications, such as 132 SMs and 128 CUDA cores per SM, reflecting interest in hardware capabilities.
